# docrot

> docrot finds where documentation lies about the code. It extracts every claim a Markdown document makes about a repository (file paths, Go/Odin/Python symbols, CLI flags, environment variables, config keys, heading anchors, shell commands, Go import paths), checks each against the real code, uses git history to flag sections whose referenced code churned after the prose was last edited, and compares bilingual document pairs for structural drift. Single static Go binary, standard library only.

Module `docrot`, Go 1.26. Entry point `cmd/docrot`. All logic lives under `internal/`.

## Commands

- `docrot check [dir]` — scan, report, exit 1 when a new finding reaches `--fail-on` (default error). Formats: text (default; info hidden unless `--info`), md, json, sarif, html.
- Every `docrot check` also rewrites the `outDir` directory (a dot-directory at the repo root by default, excluded from discovery, self-ignoring via its own `.gitignore`) with the same report in all four formats; the Markdown one is written for agents — findings grouped by file, what the severities mean, and a fix checklist. `--out-dir` moves it, `--no-out` skips it.
- `docrot explain <doc>` — every reference extracted from one document with kind, confidence and verdict. Use it before writing ignore rules.
- `docrot baseline [dir]` — freeze current findings into `.docrot-baseline.json`; later runs only fail on new ones.
- `docrot coverage [dir]` — exported symbols / flags / env vars never mentioned by any document.
- `docrot pairs [dir]` — only the source/translation checks.
- `docrot index [dir] --kind symbols|flags|env|paths|anchors|config|odin|python` — dump an index.
- `docrot init [dir]` — write a default `.docrot.json`.

## Pipeline (one package per stage)

- `internal/markdown` — line-oriented tokenizer: headings (GitHub slugs, CJK-safe), fences, code spans, links, images, tables, HTML comments, `docrot:ignore` directives, structural fingerprint for pairs.
- `internal/extract` — tokens → `model.Reference` with a kind and a confidence (high/medium/low). Heuristics are in `classify.go` (spans, links, prose) and `fences.go` (shell and Go blocks).
- `internal/index` — composite `model.Index` over `index/files`, `index/gosym` (go/parser: packages, symbols, methods, fields, flags, env reads, json/yaml/toml tag paths, exported surface), `index/odin`, `index/py`, `index/anchors`, `index/config` (JSON sample keys).
- `internal/resolve` — per-kind resolvers producing `model.Finding` with did-you-mean suggestions (`internal/fuzzy`, git rename history, sibling repos).
- `internal/gitx` — git CLI wrapper: blame line times, commits since, renames, check-ignore; cached, bounded concurrency, graceful when git is absent.
- `internal/stale` — section edit time (blame) vs churn of referenced files (log).
- `internal/pairs` — pair detection (`{stem}-zh.md` patterns, en/zh directory conventions, explicit config) and fingerprint diff; `pair-lag` via git.
- `internal/coverage` — documented vs exported.
- `internal/baseline` — fingerprints exclude line numbers.
- `internal/report` — text, agent-facing markdown, json, sarif 2.1.0, self-contained html.
- `internal/engine` — orchestration; `cmd/docrot` — CLI and exit codes.

## Contracts

- `internal/model` is the only shared package: `Kind`, `Confidence`, `Severity`, `Reference`, `Finding`, rule ids, `Index` interface.
- Severity policy: paths/anchors/commands/imports/symbols follow confidence (high→error, medium→warning, low→info); flags and env are one step softer; config keys and glob misses are info; bare file names are info.
- Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 findings at/above `--fail-on`, 2 usage/config/internal error.
- Config: `.docrot.json` (see README). Notable keys: `exclude`, `ignore` (regexes on reference text), `siblings` (other repos where paths may live), `stale.exclude`, `severity`, `pairs`, `pairPatterns`.
